_note: Hadith-card assignments, companions line. Written 2026-08-24 by tools/select_hadith_cards.py plus judgement. Every `text` is quoted verbatim from the fixed edition named in `work`; `ref` is the work's own internal number, never a page. `confidence` is the selector's, not a scholar's — every row below `high` is on the verification worklist in 00-foundations/hadith-verification-worklist.md. Chain numbers apply the standing proposal: grouped by the Masoom pointed to, in historical order, numbered independently of the silsila. Audited 2026-08-24 by tools/verify_hadith_assignments.py, which proves each saying is really in a held source at the reference given.

assignments.ref: short maxims of the Prophet, no. 165
assignments.text: Regard your relatives even by means of mere greeting.

assignments.ref: short maxims of the Prophet, no. 99
assignments.text: Faith is two halves; one half is lying in patience and the other in thankfulness.

assignments.ref: short maxims of the Prophet, no. 40
assignments.text: Ask the scholars, speak with the wise, and sit with the poor.

assignments.theme: holding on when it is not safe to
assignments.ref: short maxims of the Prophet, no. 126
assignments.text: The most intelligent of people are the most fearful of God and the most obedient to Him. The most unintelligent of people are the most fearful of the rulers and the most obedient to them.
assignments.verified_note: Replaced with Prophet saying no. 126. It praises fearing God over rulers, perfectly matching Sumayyah's historic refusal to yield to Abu Jahl.

assignments.ref: short maxims of the Prophet, no. 164
assignments.text: It is illicit to violate anything of the believer: his honor, wealth, and blood—all are sanctified.

assignments.theme: care that lasts a whole life
assignments.ref: vol. 4, hadith 872
assignments.text: Hearts are naturally inclined to love those who do good to them and to dislike those who harm them.
assignments.verified_note: Replaced with the Faqih vol. 4, hadith 872 translation. It is the same saying as Tuhaf no. 17 but uses much simpler vocabulary suitable for an 8-year-old ('love', 'do good', 'dislike', 'harm' instead of 'abhorring'/'nastily').

assignments.theme: kindness to a child in your care
assignments.ref: short maxims of the Prophet, no. 95
assignments.text: Kindness gives embellishment to everything it joins, and clumsiness ruins everything it joins.

assignments.ref: vol. 2, hadith 869
assignments.text: First the companion, then the journey.
assignments.verified_note: Replaced with the Prophet's saying from Man Lā Yaḥḍuruh al-Faqīh (vol. 2, hadith 869): 'First the companion, then the journey.' The current saying 'The proper fulfillment of the pledges...' is formal and dry for an 8-year-old, whereas the new saying is simple, memorable, and highlights the theme of lifelong loyalty and shared travel (migrations) that defined Asma's companion role.

assignments.ref: short maxims of Imam Ali, no. 104
assignments.text: No one will find the true taste of faith before he neglects telling lies whether seriously or jokingly.

assignments.theme: service, and what a servant is owed
assignments.ref: short maxims of Imam Ali, no. 62
assignments.text: Do you not know that walking with the rider ruins the manners of the rider and humiliate the walker? Leave me now.
assignments.verified_note: Replaced with Imam Ali's saying from Tuhaf (short maxims, no. 62): 'Do you not know that walking with the rider ruins the manners of the rider and humiliate the walker? Leave me now.' The current saying 'Every powerful that is under God's control is humble' was a low-confidence weak match on 'humble', whereas this new saying directly matches Qambar's theme of master-servant dignity, condemning the humiliation of a walking servant by a riding master.

assignments.ref: Saying 52
assignments.text: The most capable of pardoning is he who is the most powerful to punish.
assignments.verified_note: Replaced with Imam Ali's saying from Nahj al-Balagha (no. 52): 'The most capable of pardoning is he who is the most powerful to punish.' The current saying 'People's similarity to their rulers...' was about imitation rather than gentleness, whereas this saying perfectly captures the gentleness and restraint of a powerful commander like Malik al-Ashtar. | 2026-08-24 audit: confirmed at 'Hadith n. 52 / 52. Amir al-mu'minin said:' in the fixed edition. Ref changed from 'no. 52' to 'Saying 52' and the translator spelling normalised to the fixed record.

assignments.theme: raising a child who is not your own
assignments.ref: Letter 47
assignments.text: Keep Allāh in view in the matter of orphans. So do not allow them to starve and they should not be ruined in your presence.
assignments.verified_note: Replaced with Imam Ali's saying from Nahj al-Balagha (Letter 47 / hadith 1436): 'Keep Allāh in view in the matter of orphans. So do not allow them to starve and they should not be ruined in your presence.' The current saying 'A true friend is...' was a low-confidence match on friendship, whereas this saying perfectly matches Fatima bint Asad's theme of raising an orphan (the Prophet) and feeding him before her own children. | 2026-08-24 audit: IS in the fixed edition, Letter 47 (the will to Hasan and Husayn). Four searches missed it because that PDF prints 'orphaus' — a scanning artifact. The word is corrected to 'orphans' on the authority of the Thaqalayn copy of the SAME translation, which prints it correctly. Two witnesses to one translator, so this is a restoration, not a silent edit.

assignments.ref: short maxims of Imam al-Hasan, no. 6
assignments.text: He who depends upon God's good option for him will not wish to be in a situation other than that which God opts for him.

assignments.theme: a trust kept when nobody would have known
assignments.ref: short maxims of Imam al-Husayn, no. 3

assignments.theme: the truth said in front of a ruler
assignments.ref: short maxims of Imam al-Husayn, no. 19
assignments.text: He who tries to achieve something through acting disobediently to God will miss what he expects and fall in what he fears.
assignments.verified_note: Promoted to high because the saying is a strong match for her theme (standing up to Yazid), warning that those who seek goals through disobeying God will fall into what they fear.

assignments.ref: short maxims of Imam al-Sajjad, no. 23
assignments.text: Many are those whom are deceived by commendation…

assignments.theme: keeping a trust across a lifetime
assignments.ref: short maxims of Imam al-Baqir, no. 56
assignments.text: Abide by piety, diligence, honesty, and fulfillment of the trusts of the charitable as well as the sinful. If the killer of Ali Ibn Abi Talib ('a) deposits with me a trust, I will surely keep it for him.
assignments.verified_note: 2026-08-24 audit: restored the second sentence rather than adding an ellipsis. It is the whole point of the saying and the reason it matches Jabir's theme; cutting it left the generic half.

assignments.theme: knowledge, whatever the age of the one holding it
assignments.ref: short maxims of Imam al-Sadiq, no. 77
assignments.text: Everything has its tax and the tax of knowledge is to teach its people.

assignments.ref: vol. 4, hadith 19
assignments.text: Be good to your parents, and your children will be good to you.
assignments.verified_note: Replaced with Imam al-Sadiq's saying from Man Lā Yaḥḍuruh al-Faqīh (vol. 4, hadith 19): 'Be good to your parents, and your children will be good to you.' The current saying 'A twenty-year friendship is kinship' was a low-confidence match on friendship, whereas this saying is a direct, child-friendly maxim about honouring parents, perfectly matching Umm Farwa's theme.

assignments.ref: short maxims of Imam al-Kadhim, no. 20
assignments.text: The expiation of working with the (unjust) rulers is to treat the friends with kindness.

assignments.theme: teaching, and who is fit to teach
assignments.blocker: Text found and perfect — 'learn whatever you ignore and teach the ignorant your knowledge', in Imam al-Kadhim's commandment to Hisham. But that commandment is unnumbered prose in Tuhaf, and sourcing-rules.md forbids a citation without a number. al-Kafi vol. 1 hadith 13 carries a Hisham sermon but not this clause. Needs a numbered edition of the commandment, or a different saying.

specimen.text: Anyone who acknowledges God should not complain when his earnings are delayed and should not accuse God of His acts.
specimen.why: Real attributed saying of the same Masoom, NOT theme-verified. Present so the card can be proofed at true length.

assignments.ref: short maxims of Imam al-Rida, no. 13
assignments.text: When you want to mention a present person, you should use his surname, but when you refer to an absent person, you should use his name.
assignments.verified_note: 2026-08-24 audit: the previous selection quoted Rida no. 24 as 'The limit of trusting in God IS to fear nobody except Him'. The edition prints 'IN to fear' — a typo, and unlike Letter 47 there is no second witness, because Tuhaf exists in this project in one copy only. Correcting it would be an unattested emendation, so the row reverts to no. 13. FINDING FOR THE HUMANS: none of the three speech-adjacent Rida maxims fits 'saying the thing out loud'; the theme may be wrong for the material rather than the saying being wrong for the theme.

assignments.theme: family, and the road toward it
assignments.ref: short maxims of Imam al-Rida, no. 10
assignments.text: The elder brother is as same as the father.
assignments.verified_note: Promoted to high. The saying 'The elder brother is as same as the father' is a perfect, direct fit for Sayyida Ma'suma's theme of family and her long journey to reach her elder brother, Imam al-Rida.

assignments.ref: short maxims of Imam al-Jawad, no. 13
assignments.text: A believer is in need of successfulness from God, a self-preaching, and accession to the advisers.

assignments.ref: short maxims of Imam al-Hadi, no. 10
assignments.text: The thankful of a grace should be happy for thankfulness more than it is for the grace.

assignments.ref: short maxims of Imam al-Askari, no. 33
assignments.text: Those who advice their friends secretly are respecting them, and those who advice them openly are humiliating them.

assignments.ref: short maxims of Imam al-Askari, no. 20
assignments.text: The faithful believer is a blessing for the believers and a claim against the disbelievers.
assignments.note: Also carries the prior undecided question of whether this entry points to Imam al-Hadi or Imam al-Askari. Assigned to al-Askari here because he served as al-Askari's wakil into the occultation; if that call goes the other way the card changes.
